outcome: The general Berry-Tabor conjecture remains open, but two new cases were settled in the window: Kim, Marklof and Welsh (Jan 2026) proved the two-point Poisson spectral statistics for a quantum particle in a 3-dimensional rectangular box under a Diophantine condition on the side-length ratios, extending Eskin-Margulis-Mozes's 2005 two-dimensional result; and Lutsko (Sep 2026) proved Poissonian pair correlation for the relative spectrum of the three-particle trigonometric Sutherland model (an interacting many-body integrable system) under a Diophantine condition on the coupling constant, the first such result for an interacting system at the pair-correlation level.
summary: The Berry-Tabor conjecture (1977) asserts that generic integrable quantum systems have Poisson local spectral statistics, contrasting with random-matrix statistics for chaotic systems. It remains open in general as of September 2026, but the triage's lead — Kim, Marklof and Welsh, 'Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori' (arXiv:2601.03209, submitted 2026-01-06, v1 only) — checks out: they prove the two-point spectral density statement of the conjecture for a quantum particle in a 3-dimensional rectangular box under a Diophantine condition (κ close to 1) on the ratios of squared side lengths ℓᵢ²/ℓⱼ², extending the 2-dimensional case proved by Eskin, Margulis and Mozes in 2005 (which predates the window and is the prior state of the art, not a new event). This is a case of the general conjecture — a restriction to a specific class of integrable systems (rectangular 3-tori) under a technical Diophantine hypothesis — not a resolution, so it is classified `partial` with direction `confirmed` (the result confirms the conjectured Poisson statistics, it does not refute them). I additionally found a second, independent case settled within the window: Christopher Lutsko, 'Poissonian pair correlations for the three-particle Sutherland model' (arXiv:2609.03112, submitted 2026-09-02), which proves the conjecture's pair-correlation statement for a genuinely interacting integrable many-body system (three particles on a circle with inverse-square chord interaction) under a Diophantine condition on the coupling constant — described as the first such result for an interacting system at the pair-correlation level, reducing to Marklof's theorem on inhomogeneous quadratic forms via a finite-congruence/Weyl-sector argument. I checked both papers' full text/HTML and found no mention of AI, machine learning, automated theorem proving, or computer-assisted search in either the body or acknowledgements; both are conventional analytic-number-theory/homogeneous-dynamics proofs (Ratner theory, unipotent flows, quadratic form equidistribution). I also checked a third item the triage did not surface, arXiv:2605.06974 ('Poissonian correlations of α n^d mod 1' by Lutsko, Rome and Technau), which is a related-but-distinct problem (polynomial sequences mod 1, a number-theoretic analogue rather than a statement about quantum spectra of an integrable system) and does not count as a case of this bullet; I did not rely on it for status. The Wikipedia article on the conjecture, fetched directly, still describes it as open and mentions no recent proofs or AI, consistent with the frozen revision's framing and giving no reason to revise `status_sources` beyond the primary arXiv papers.
competing_reading: One could argue the 3-tori and Sutherland-model results are 'related problems' (different underlying integrable system) rather than 'cases' of the single conjecture as stated in the Wikipedia bullet, since the bullet's wording is generic ('generic integrable quantum systems') and doesn't specify a system. But per the DEEP_DIVE.md scope rule, restricting the general conjecture to a specific, well-defined sub-class of integrable systems (a class of tori, a class of many-body Hamiltonians) under an explicit Diophantine restriction is exactly the kind of restriction that counts as a case, not a variant — the underlying question (are the level statistics Poisson for this integrable system) is unchanged, only the system considered is narrowed. I judge `partial` is the correct reading, but flag this because the bullet names no specific system, unlike some Wikipedia bullets that name a precise sub-case.
what_would_settle_it: A full resolution of the Berry-Tabor conjecture would require proving Poisson statistics for a genuinely general class of 'generic' integrable systems (not restricted to Diophantine sub-families of tori or specific many-body models), or a counterexample showing genericity fails. Absent that, the record stands as `partial` with each new proved case adding to `status_sources`.
